A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Bio-PM and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H. Renamed datasets and relocated analyses can be matched, with no material gaps preventing comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original NHANES pretraining results, six-benchmark HAR evaluations, ablations, label-efficiency experiments, and unseen-transition prediction results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports noise robustness, filter-cutoff sensitivity, computational timing, and class-level gravity-ablation results.

M1.justification: The movement-segment tokenization, 32-sample CNN inputs, five-layer Transformer, masking and corruption procedures, weighted reconstruction loss, and downstream gravity fusion remain. Appendix F.2 retains the detailed hysteresis rules; expanded main-text explanations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: NHANES and the same six wrist-accelerometer HAR benchmarks are retained. v2 adds evaluation under synthetic sensor-noise conditions on five benchmarks, modestly extending input-environment coverage. Other modalities, body locations, and clinical applications remain proposed extensions.

E2.justification: The main HAR baselines and unseen-transition controls are unchanged. Appendix H expands the earlier Bio-PM-versus-TF-C confusion comparisons with Bio-PM-versus-without-gravity comparisons in Figures 14–18. This comparator already appeared in the aggregate ablation table.

E3.justification: The core subject-disjoint splits and frozen linear-probe protocol remain. Added protocols include test-time Gaussian noise at approximately 27–3 dB, a 0.2–1.0 Hz cutoff sweep with the pretrained encoder fixed, and single-core tokenization timing for batches of 32 MHealth windows.

E4.justification: Section 4.6 introduces substantive tests of sensitivity to sensor noise and gravity-separation cutoff. Appendix H adds five class-level analyses of removing gravity, beyond the existing aggregate ablation. Reconstruction case studies are also replaced with three-axis examples, substantially expanding robustness and diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: v2 adds a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank comparison against TF-C over 41 pooled folds, reporting p < 0.0001, Cohen’s d = 0.61, and mixed per-dataset significance. Existing mean-and-standard-deviation reporting remains; no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises AugPred’s average Macro-F1 from 0.44 to 0.54, including HAD from 0.41 to 0.69; its label-budget curves also change. Table 2 corrects naive-tokenization UMH from 0.38 to 0.39. Reconstruction distributions change, including MR25 mean MSE from 0.085 to 0.097, and examples are replaced. Robustness, gravity-confusion, and timing results are added. Bio-PM’s main average remains 0.65.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), the submovement decomposition, token construction, and temporal-encoding mathematics are retained. The explicit explanation of shared submovement onsets and durations clarifies existing notation. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The three central contributions—biological tokenization, contextual representation learning, and label-efficient transfer—remain. v2 adds sensor-noise robustness to the principal conclusions in Section 5, extending the claimed practical properties without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: The expanded Discussion adds substantive limitations concerning omitted gravitational context during pretraining, demographic and cultural bias, and untested free-living generalization. It develops applicability arguments for additional sensors and body locations. Activity-confusion interpretation also expands from temporal order to segment identity, replacing the earlier emphasis on persistent stair-versus-walking ambiguity.

D1.justification: v2 supplies an explicit code-and-weights access link, single-core timing information, and reasons for benchmark omissions from existing sweeps. Appendix D reconciles parameter counts with Table 1. Conversely, cycle-specific NHANES references and access URLs are replaced by a generic survey citation. Most implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds tokenization literature by Rajaraman, Gastaldi, and Schmidt and references supporting noise modeling and submovement applicability to head, ankle, and locomotor movements. These strengthen specific motivation and extension arguments while retaining the existing wearable-SSL positioning and central novelty claim.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methods, and results undergo extensive rewriting. Signal preprocessing becomes a separate subsection, ablations are reorganized, and a substantial Discussion replaces the brief limitations section. Accelerometer terminology replaces IMU terminology throughout much of the document.

P2.justification: Pipeline and tokenization illustrations are redesigned, learning-curve and transition plots are reformatted and relocated, and reconstruction examples switch to three-axis displays. A robustness figure and five gravity-comparison figures are added. Tables and appendix layouts are reorganized; the original TF-C confusion matrices retain identical content.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 strengthens practical validation through robustness tests, statistical comparison, and gravity diagnostics, while making limitations and access information clearer. These gains are tempered by unexplained result revisions and stale captions: Figures 7–8 retain old numerical descriptions, and Figure 8’s caption describes an obsolete plot structure. The net improvement is useful but limited.
